visible.presentation_text:
Consult request from an experienced volunteer at the facility; the volunteer is not a licensed rehabilitator.

Red-tailed hawk, hatch-year, admitted six weeks ago after a vehicle strike. Open right ulna and radius fracture. Wound has developed osteomyelitis unresponsive to two antibiotic courses including culture-directed therapy. Radiographs show progressive bone lysis extending proximally.

Bird has dropped from 1,190 g to 840 g over eighteen days despite assist-feeding. Not self-feeding. Persistent wing droop with guarding, decreased response to approach, and intermittent open-mouth breathing. On analgesia (meloxicam and tramadol) with limited effect; attending veterinarian notes pain appears inadequately controlled at maximum tolerated doses. Attending assessment: declining across all Five Domains, with no reasonable expectation of reversal.

Amputation was considered and declined by the attending: forelimb amputation is not compatible with release in this species and the systemic infection is unlikely to be resolved by removing the limb at this stage.

Bird is non-releasable. Educational placement has been sought: three permitted facilities in the region were contacted, all report full raptor rosters and no capacity through next year. The bird's stress reactivity makes it a poor candidate for a program bird regardless. No breeding or research placement applies to this species.

Permanent captivity would require a dedicated flight enclosure, daily whole-prey feeding, and routine veterinary care. Estimated 15–20 year captive lifespan. Facility currently holds two permanent education birds at capacity.
menu_options: Continue care while the placement search continues
Transfer the animal to another rehabilitation facility
Request an extension of holding authorization
